title: Tanzanian Grilled Banana
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Ndizi ya Kuchoma — small Tanzanian finger bananas grilled directly over charcoal until the skin blackens and the flesh inside caramelises. The simplest highland street snack — sweet, smoky, and completely natural.
longDesc: Grilled finger bananas are the snack of Tanzania's highland regions where bananas grow abundantly. Smaller and sweeter than plantains, they need only minutes over charcoal to become magnificently caramelised.
ingredients: 8 small ripe finger bananas or standard bananas
steps: Place whole unpeeled ripe bananas directly on charcoal.
Grill 5—6 minutes until the skin is completely blackened.
Skin should be fully blackened; the banana inside soft and caramelised.
Slit and eat directly from the skin.
chefTips: Ripe yellow bananas only — green ones remain starchy.
The blacker the skin, the better the caramelisation inside.
cookingScience: See TZA181 for grilled plantain cooking science — the same chemistry applies to bananas, with the added factor that dessert bananas contain more sucrose and fructose than starchy plantains, producing even more rapid and dramatic caramelisation.
sustainabilityTips: Bananas are one of Tanzania's most abundant fruits — zero waste.
culturalNote: Grilled finger bananas are the highland market snack — sold at the Kilimanjaro foothills markets, the Arusha vegetable stalls, and every highland bus stop. They are the simplest possible street food and among the most satisfying.
